name: The Verge
look: Near-black editorial canvas with acid-mint and ultraviolet as hazard tape, brutally heavy display type, saturated colour-block story tiles.

hero.title: THE SYNTH THAT ATE THE INTERNET
hero.sub: A €400 box from a four-person workshop in Ghent has a fourteen-month waiting list, and the people running it are not sure they want the orders.

items.title: The chip nobody can buy
items.body: Allocation for the new accelerator was spoken for eighteen months before tape-out. We asked eleven buyers how that happened.

items.title: Launch delayed again

items.title: The cable landing fight
items.body: A town of 4,000 people is deciding where a third of a continent's bandwidth comes ashore.

items.title: What the demo left out

showcases.title: THE CABLE LANDING FIGHT
showcases.body: A fishing town of four thousand people on the Irish coast is deciding where a third of a continent's internet traffic comes ashore. The hearings have been running for nine months, and almost nobody outside the town has been watching.
points: Nine months of hearings, attended in person
Interviews with eleven residents and four operators
Route maps obtained under freedom of information

showcases.title: WHAT THE DEMO LEFT OUT
showcases.body: We ran the keynote prompts on the same hardware configuration, in the same order, and recorded the wall-clock time for each. Three of the eight results do not reproduce, and one is off by a factor of four.
points: Same hardware, same prompts, same order
Full methodology and raw timings published
Vendor given seventy-two hours to respond

palette.name: Jelly Mint
palette.note: Signature acid-mint accent — CTA fill, link underlines, active tab borders, high-attention tiles

palette.name: Verge Ultraviolet
palette.note: The complementary brand hazard — secondary colour-block tiles and outlined buttons

palette.name: Console Mint Border
palette.note: Darker mint for card outlines and button borders where pure mint over-saturates

palette.name: Deep Link Blue
palette.note: The link hover colour — the one moment blue appears on the site

palette.name: Focus Cyan
palette.note: Button focus rings. Never shown outside a keyboard-focus state

palette.name: Purple Rule
palette.note: Darker ultraviolet used as the vertical border on StoryStream items

palette.name: Canvas Black
palette.note: The default dark surface — warm enough to read as a newsprint negative, not an OLED void

palette.name: Surface Slate
palette.note: Secondary card background when a tile does not need to be a colour block

palette.name: Hazard White
palette.note: Story-tile fill, button border and primary text — a white block is an editorial spotlight

palette.name: Absolute Black
palette.note: Text on mint, yellow and white tiles — the only place it appears

palette.name: Secondary Text
palette.note: Bylines, timestamps, photo credits — the metadata layer

palette.name: Muted Text
palette.note: Button text on dark slate buttons, slightly off-white to reduce glare

notes: There is no light mode. The dark canvas is the product; the palette only inverts when a single tile takes a mint, yellow or white fill.
Mint and ultraviolet are hazard tape, not background wash. One saturated block per screen region, never two competing.
Story tiles are rounded 20–40px and filled edge to edge with colour, stacked on a dashed vertical rule like commits in a log.
Depth is entirely flat — 1px hairlines in white, mint or ultraviolet do the work shadows would do elsewhere.
Black text appears only on mint, yellow or white tiles. Everywhere else text is white or the #949494 metadata grey.
